$comment: THE EXPLICIT HARNESS LIST. scripts/run-harnesses.cjs runs exactly these files and nothing else.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: on 17 September 2026 a verification sweep written as `ls scripts/*.cjs` ran
scripts/migrate-from-sheets.cjs against the LIVE database with the service role — 132 rows of
public.discovery_trucks overwritten and 19 inserted in 1.2 seconds. See
docs/discovery-upsert-incident-report.md. A glob cannot tell a proof from a migration; a list can.
RULE: never glob scripts/. Add a new harness HERE or the runner will report it as unregistered.

excluded.$comment: Every other scripts/*.cjs file, with the reason it is NOT in the list above. The runner checks this covers the directory.

operational_refused.$why: Builds a real client and WRITES to production. The runner refuses these by source inspection even if someone lists one.

operational_read_only.$why: Talks to live Stripe/Supabase. Read-only today, but it is an operational tool, not a proof, and it must never run unattended.

server.$why: A long-running local TCP server. It never exits, so a sequential runner would hang on it (it held the 17 Sep sweep for 200s).

shared_modules.$why: Required BY the harnesses. They export helpers and assert nothing, so running them proves nothing.

fixture_generators.$why: 🔴 THESE REWRITE THE COMMITTED GOLDEN FIXTURES. Running them in a sweep would silently regenerate the baseline that batch-rolling-identity.cjs and batch-reservation-golden-on.cjs check AGAINST, turning both proofs into tautologies. Run by hand, deliberately, only from a build whose harnesses already pass.

one_off_tools.$why: 🔴 PROVISIONING AND DOCUMENT TOOLS, NOT PROOFS. `_fetch-weekly-post-fonts.cjs` downloads the pinned font files into assets/ (a network fetch, run once and committed); `_weekly-post-examples.cjs` writes the example posters that appear in the report. Both WRITE FILES INTO THE REPOSITORY, which is exactly what a sweep must not do: running them would rewrite committed bytes and could quietly change what the weekly-post harness measures against. Run by hand, deliberately.

needs_a_browser.$why: 🔴 NOT A PROOF THE SWEEP CAN RUN. It needs `.next/static/css` from a completed build and a local Chromium, and a sweep that silently skips when either is missing would be a sweep that reports green for a layout nobody measured. Most are a MODULE (`outreach-workspace-v3-fixes.cjs` requires one behind HG_RENDER=1) and a standalone command; run them by hand after a build. ⚠️ `add-order-stale-browser.cjs` is the stricter case and its own header says so: it needs the DEV SERVER, the Supabase project and an operator session, so it can never be swept — it is run by hand against test-truck with the token in the environment. ⚠️ `social-posts-render.cjs` (6 October 2026) and `social-tab-render.cjs` (7 October 2026) are listed here for the same reason: both need `.next/static` and a local Chromium AND a local WebKit. ⚠️ `caption-chips-render.cjs` (10 October 2026) needs the two browsers but NOT a build: it loads the compiled `lib/weekly-post/caption-chips.ts` into a file:// page and presses a REAL Backspace against a REAL contenteditable. 🔴 IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE ENGINES DISAGREE — deleting a chip cleared the whole template in Safari, the component's own comment claimed every engine treats a non-editable inline span as one character, and no source check and no single-engine test was ever going to find that. ⛔ `places-tab-render.cjs` was DELETED with the Places tab it measured. ⛔ `schedule-places-render.cjs` WAS DELETED ON 7 OCTOBER 2026 and this is its tombstone: it measured the Schedule tab's three sub-tab pills, the Places pane and the Add event modal, and two of those three no longer exist — Schedule is two pills and Places is Social media › Locations. What survives of its job is `social-tab-render.cjs`, which measures the same shapes on the screens they moved to, in Chromium AND WebKit. ⚠️ `social-posts-render.cjs` LOST THREE OF ITS FOUR FIXTURES the same day, for the same reason — Social posts' three boxes, the per-location design editor and the picture library page are all gone — and kept the shared DESIGN EDITOR and the FONT PICKER, which are unchanged screens. ⚠️ IT WAS REPAIRED THE DAY BEFORE IT WAS DELETED, which is worth recording rather than hiding: it had not run at all for days, the repair found that, and the next day's brief retired the screens it was aimed at. See docs/social-tab-report.md. ⚠️ `social-tab-5-local.cjs` (9 October 2026) is the add-order case again and is listed for the same reason its header gives: it needs `next dev` on :3000 AND the Supabase project, because it asks the RUNNING route questions rather than reading source. 🔴 IT IS WORTH ITS BY-HAND COST: it is how the `asSlotName` default was found, where `place_slot_clear` with an unknown slot name answered 200 having cleared a real location’s picture — a default no source check was going to notice. ⛔ IT WRITES ONLY TO `id = 'test-truck'`, looked up by that id, and deletes nothing. ⚠️ `social-tab-6-local.cjs` (10 October 2026) JOINS IT RATHER THAN REPLACING IT, which is a departure from the one-per-round habit and is deliberate: round 5's script asks the ROUTE about captions and picture slots and round 6's is about THE EDITOR, so neither covers the other. 🔴 ROUND 6's SECOND HALF MOUNTS THE REAL `DesignEditor` with react-dom/client on `scripts/_mini-dom.cjs` and drives its real handlers, because the dashboard is behind a login this script has no session for — so a corner drag is `DraggableBox`'s own `onPointerDown`, and what it produced is read back out of the editor's own SAVE. ⛔ IT SAVES NOTHING TO THE DATABASE: `onSave` is the harness's own callback, and the live half only READS. ⚠️ `live-poster.cjs` (10 October 2026 · §2) needs the two browsers but NOT a build and NOT a server: it renders the poster twice — once through satori and once by mounting the SAME `El[]` tree in a real browser — and compares the pixels with the DOM. 🔴 IT IS THE ONLY CHECK THAT CAN ANSWER §2's REAL QUESTION. The source harnesses can see that the editor CALLS `weeklyTree`; only this can say whether the words land where the PNG puts them, and a live stage that is fast and wrong is worse than the slow one it replaced. ⚠️ IT ALSO FOUND THAT "Line spacing" MEASURED AND NEVER DREW, and its control is what proves the fix. 🔴 `live-text-place.cjs` (10 October 2026 · §2, after the operator reported the words in the wrong place) IS THE STRICTEST OF THE THREE AND THE ONLY ONE THAT COULD HAVE CAUGHT THAT BUG: it bundles the REAL `DesignEditor` with esbuild, mounts it in WebKit and Chromium over a tiny local HTTP server that answers the font GET with the committed Oswald file, and measures each box outline against the rectangles of the words drawn for it — at five widths and three zoom levels. ⛔ THE OTHER HARNESSES COULD NOT SEE IT: the source ones read code, `live-poster.cjs` compares the TREE with the PNG (and the tree was right), and `social-tab-6-local.cjs` mounts the editor on a mini-DOM WITH NO LAYOUT ENGINE, so "where is this box on screen" is not a question it can be asked. ⚠️ It needs `.next/static` for the app stylesheet and the two browsers; its control declares the blank at twice the layout’s size and 45 words fall outside their boxes.
